name: Orca
title: Ninebrains vs Orca
description: Ninebrains vs Orca, the open-source agent development environment for running Claude Code, Codex and other agents in parallel worktrees: remotes, telemetry, planning and checks.
summary: MIT, cross-platform, worktree per agent, strong on remotes and cloud VMs.
answer: Orca and Ninebrains are both free, open-source, cross-platform apps that run Claude Code, Codex and other agents in parallel, each in its own git worktree. Choose Orca for SSH hosts, cloud VMs, a mobile companion and very broad agent support. Choose Ninebrains for a dependency-aware job graph, checks that block completion until they pass, and no telemetry.

what.text: An agent development environment that runs Claude Code, Codex and any other coding agent in parallel.

price.text: Free, using your own agent subscriptions.

agents.text: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Grok and any other agent CLI.

isolation.text: A git worktree per agent, locally, on an SSH host or in a cloud VM.

planning.text: Coordinator agents that run worker agents, and task intake from GitHub and Linear. A dependency graph is not described.

verification.text: Diff review with line notes sent back to the agent, and failing checks or PR comments sent back to fix.

telemetry.text: Anonymous usage telemetry with no content, which you can turn off in Settings or with DO_NOT_TRACK=1.

chooseThem.text: You want agents on SSH hosts or a cloud VM per worktree, still running while your laptop sleeps.
You want agents to drive Orca itself from the command line: create worktrees, start workers, schedule automations.
You want an MIT licence and a very fast release cadence.

chooseUs: You want jobs with dependencies, handed to idle lanes as they unblock.
You want completion blocked until configured checks pass, before you review, with three attempts before a job blocks.
You want no telemetry at all, rather than anonymous telemetry you opt out of.
